docs.title: Clichy engineering guide
docs.text:
Clichy is a self-hosted photo library service developed for ECAM Brussels Project 2026. This site documents the implementation visible in this repository, the current Kubernetes and CI configuration, and the gaps against the assignment. It is intended for developers, operators, and evaluation preparation.

Repository state, not a live cluster audit

Statements about implementation are based on the checked-out source and Git history. Unless explicitly stated, this documentation has not verified the current state of a live cluster. See the requirements matrix for status definitions.

Start with the project overview, then follow developer onboarding. Operators should read the Kubernetes environments, deployment runbook, and database migration guide.

The observed checkout is master at 2a7717f (2026-11-15). The app currently contains a web UI, authenticated API, filesystem photo storage, image metadata and hashing, and asynchronous processing. PostgreSQL and Redis are each configured as one instance per namespace. Database replication and sharding are not configured.

docs.title: Web
docs.text: apps/web is a React Router application built with Vite. File-system route setup is in apps/web/src/routes.ts; visible routes include index, login, and dashboard. Components include login/sign-up forms and user menu. The browser API origin is supplied through VITE_SERVER_URL; production image build currently passes http://localhost:3000, so deployments that need another public API origin must review the build argument and routing assumptions.

docs.title: API and authentication
docs.text:
apps/server/src/index.ts creates a Fastify server on port 3000, enables multipart uploads (20 MiB maximum), CORS with credentials, exposes /metrics, mounts photo routes, and adapts Better Auth under /api/auth/*. Better Auth uses Prisma/PostgreSQL and email/password auth. Fastify's logger is enabled. Route handlers return explicit errors for unauthenticated requests, missing input, unsupported images, and missing records; unexpected errors are passed to Fastify's handler.

Key routes in apps/server/src/routes/photos.ts:

Method/path Purpose GET /photos List the authenticated user's photos POST /photos Validate and save upload; create record and return 202 pending processing GET /photos/:id/metadata Read metadata for an owned photo GET /photos/:id/thumbnail/:variant Read an owned derivative variant GET /photos/:id Retrieve original photo content GET /photos/:id/duplicates Find exact SHA-256 matches owned by the user GET /photos/:id/similar Rank candidates by pHash distance; accepts threshold and limit DELETE /photos/:id Delete an owned photo and its stored files

Auth route surface is Better Auth's handler; consult packages/auth/src/index.ts and Better Auth config for exact behavior.

docs.title: Image pipeline
docs.text:
apps/server/src/image-processing.ts validates and decodes JPEG, PNG, WebP, and GIF using Sharp with a 40-million-pixel cap. It extracts optional EXIF via Exifr, generates SHA-256 and a 64-bit DCT perceptual hash, and writes resized WebP variants. pHash comparison uses Hamming distance in query helpers; this is a similarity primitive, not evidence of a complete duplicate review interface. Video support was not found.

apps/server/src/storage.ts implements local filesystem storage. Production mounts the same photos PVC into API and worker. This storage design makes shared writable filesystem semantics a runtime dependency.

docs.title: Error handling and logging
docs.text: Fastify logger handles API logs; worker logs structured JSON to stdout/stderr. Image validation errors and missing original files are permanent BullMQ failures; other errors can retry. Tests are Node test runner via tsx --test; test files are colocated in server and worker packages. No dedicated lint script is declared at root.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant API as Fastify API
  participant DB as PostgreSQL
  participant D as Outbox dispatcher (in API)
  participant R as Redis / BullMQ
  participant W as Worker
  participant FS as Photo filesystem
  U->>API: POST /photos (multipart)
  API->>API: Validate image and persist original
  API->>DB: Transaction: photo row + outbox row
  API-->>U: 202 Accepted, PENDING
  D->>DB: Read unpublished outbox batch
  D->>R: Add process-photo with stable job ID
  D->>DB: Mark event published (or retain error)
  R->>W: Deliver job
  W->>DB: Atomically claim PENDING/FAILED photo
  W->>FS: Read original; write derivatives
  W->>DB: Store EXIF, dimensions, hashes, COMPLETED

The outbox reduces the chance that a database photo row is committed while its queue event is lost. Dispatcher logic is in apps/server/src/queues/outbox-dispatcher.ts; upload transaction is wired in apps/server/src/routes/photos.ts. A stable SHA-256-derived job ID makes repeated publication idempotent at the queue identity level.

BullMQ defaults: four attempts, exponential backoff starting at 2 seconds, completed job retention up to one day/1000 jobs, failed up to seven days/5000 jobs. These can be set using PHOTO_JOB_ATTEMPTS, PHOTO_JOB_BACKOFF_MS; queue name defaults to photo-processing. Worker concurrency supports 1 or 2 in code; current overlays set 1.

Worker marks invalid images or missing originals as terminal failures, and transient errors return the photo to pending for retry. The server dispatcher retries failed outbox publication; it runs every two seconds, recovers processing records older than 15 minutes and pending records older than 10 minutes, and removes published outbox rows after seven days. Redis uses AOF and a PVC in Kubernetes; it is still a single Redis instance without replication. No independent outbox process or Redis failover is configured.

The worker exposes HTTP health on port 3001 (/ready returns readiness), but the inspected Deployment does not configure worker probes. Tests cover job behavior and outbox dispatch/recovery; live failure injection was not performed.

docs.title: Networking and request flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  Client[Browser / external client] -->|HTTPS: valtask.xyz or www.valtask.xyz| Cloudflare[Cloudflare edge]
  Cloudflare -->|www redirects to valtask.xyz| Canonical[Canonical host: valtask.xyz]
  Canonical -->|Cloudflare Tunnel: HTTP to Traefik port 80| Ingress[Traefik Ingress: entrypoint web]
  Ingress -->|/| WebSvc[ClusterIP clichy-web:80]
  Ingress -->|/api/auth, /photos| ApiSvc[ClusterIP clichy-server:3000]
  WebSvc --> WebPod[web Pod]
  ApiSvc --> ApiPod[server Pod]
  ApiPod -->|clichy-postgres:5432| PG[PostgreSQL Service]
  ApiPod -->|clichy-redis:6379| Redis[Redis Service]
  WorkerPod[worker Pod] --> PG
  WorkerPod --> Redis
  WorkerPod --> SharedPV[(photo PVC)]
  ApiPod --> SharedPV

The base Ingress uses Traefik class and the web entrypoint. It sends /api/auth and /photos to the API and / to web. Environment overlays change the hostname: clichy.localhost (Dev), clichy-test.home.arpa (Test), valtask.xyz (Production). In Production, the externally configured Cloudflare Tunnel forwards valtask.xyz over HTTP to Traefik on port 80; Cloudflare terminates public HTTPS. Cloudflare redirects www.valtask.xyz to https://valtask.xyz, so the Kubernetes Ingress only needs the canonical valtask.xyz host. Tunnel and redirect configuration are outside this repository. The repo's current base ingress annotation selects web; TLS configuration is not present in that Ingress.

Services use namespace-local DNS names (clichy-postgres, clichy-redis, clichy-server, clichy-web). PostgreSQL and Redis are ClusterIP internal services; no public database/Redis ingress or service is configured. For local access, use the documented ingress route or explicit kubectl port-forward only when needed.

docs.title: Network diagram caveat
docs.text: The separate Ingress resources for Grafana and Headlamp are under infra/kubernetes/monitoring and infra/kubernetes/headlamp; they are LAN-oriented configuration. They are not included in the application Ingress and are not exposed by the documented Cloudflare Tunnel. Check their host/entrypoint and cluster DNS before assuming reachability.

docs.title: Current deployment view
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  User[Browser] --> CF[Cloudflare edge: HTTPS]
  CF -->|valtask.xyz via Cloudflare Tunnel; HTTP to Traefik web :80| Traefik[Traefik Ingress]
  WWW[www.valtask.xyz] -->|Cloudflare redirect to canonical host| CF
  subgraph AppNS[Clichy-prod namespace]
    Traefik -->|/| Web[web Deployment]
    Traefik -->|/api/auth and /photos| API[server Deployment]
    API -->|Prisma| PG[(PostgreSQL StatefulSet, 1 replica)]
    API -->|BullMQ| Redis[(Redis Deployment, 1 replica + AOF PVC)]
    API -->|original + derivative files| Photos[(photos PVC)]
    API -. DB outbox dispatcher .-> Redis
    Worker[worker Deployment] --> Redis
    Worker --> PG
    Worker --> Photos
  end
  Prom[Prometheus in monitoring namespace] -. /metrics on server .-> API
  Grafana[Grafana] --> Prom

The public Production request path begins at Cloudflare. HTTPS terminates there, then the Cloudflare Tunnel forwards HTTP to Traefik's web entrypoint on port 80. www.valtask.xyz is redirected by Cloudflare to valtask.xyz; the application Ingress host is valtask.xyz. The tunnel and redirect rules are configured outside this repository. Traefik then routes the UI and API paths to their in-cluster Services.

The server is both the HTTP API and outbox dispatcher. It constructs the BullMQ queue and periodically dispatches pending outbox entries. Worker instances consume process-photo jobs. The API and worker need the same photo files; Kubernetes mounts the photos PVC into both Deployments.

docs.title: Namespace interpretation
docs.text: The repository defines clichy-dev, clichy-test, and clichy-prod; monitoring and Headlamp are separate cluster-level installations/namespaces. These are namespace boundaries on one cluster, not separate clusters. Base resources include a PostgreSQL StatefulSet and Redis Deployment; each overlay sets independent configuration and app Secrets.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Current manifests configure one server, web, worker, PostgreSQL, and Redis replica by default (Test has an HPA for server/web). PostgreSQL and Redis are single-instance services. No replication or sharding is configured. The underlying production local PVs are node-affine and do not provide node-level storage failover. No cluster or live traffic test was performed for this documentation pass.

docs.title: Repository status
docs.text: No automated PostgreSQL dump, WAL archive, snapshot schedule, restore script, or documented tested restore procedure is present in the checked-in implementation. Persistent volumes and Retain reclaim policy do not constitute a backup. Photo originals also live outside PostgreSQL and must be backed up consistently with their database references.

docs.title: Operational requirement
docs.text:
Until a validated procedure exists, treat backup/restore as an open operational gap. Design a coordinated backup covering PostgreSQL and photo storage, define retention and encryption, and test restores into an isolated namespace. Preserve Redis only as appropriate for queue recovery; the database outbox and stale-record recovery are relevant to re-enqueueing work, but are not backups.

Do not run ad hoc destructive recovery commands against Production. A future runbook should record approved tooling, consistency point, secret handling, validation queries, and recovery time/data objectives without storing credentials in the repository.

docs.title: Local workflow
docs.text:
Edit the Prisma schema, then use:

pnpm db:generate
pnpm db:migrate

The root db:migrate delegates to @clichy/db and runs prisma migrate dev; it can create a migration and prompt in development. Review and commit the generated SQL under packages/db/prisma/migrations with the schema change. pnpm db:push is available but bypasses migration history; do not use it for production changes.

Inspect migration state:

pnpm --filter @clichy/db exec prisma migrate status
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh test status
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh prod status

The environment script uses the namespace Secret and loopback port-forward. It does not print the DB URL. Running status can return nonzero when migrations are pending.

docs.title: Deployment ordering
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  SHA[Checked out SHA + matching immutable images] --> Verify[Verify clean source, node and target Secret]
  Verify --> Forward[Loopback port-forward and PostgreSQL SELECT 1]
  Forward --> Migrate[prisma migrate deploy]
  Migrate -->|success| Apply[Render and apply environment Kustomize overlay]
  Migrate -->|failure| Stop[Stop; app manifests not applied]
  Apply --> Rollout[Wait for server, web, worker rollouts]

The workflow applies migrations before deploying the matching app images. The migration script confirms the target database name (clichy_test or clichy_prod) from the connection URL and checks commit cleanliness for relevant sources. Because old Pods may serve while DDL runs, use backward-compatible expand-and-contract migrations. No transactional rollback or automatic schema rollback is provided; Prisma migration failures require diagnosis and a forward repair plan.

docs.title: PostgreSQL and Prisma
docs.text:
The current database is a standard PostgreSQL 18 single-instance StatefulSet in each app namespace. The Service name is clichy-postgres; the StatefulSet has one replica and a persistent volume claim template. Application credentials and connection URLs are injected from Kubernetes Secrets. This is not replicated PostgreSQL and Kubernetes Pod replication would not provide database replication.

Prisma 7 schema is split across packages/db/prisma/schema/auth.prisma and photo.prisma. prisma.config.ts points at the migration directory and reads DATABASE_URL; client generation outputs under packages/db/prisma/generated. createPrismaClient in packages/db/src/index.ts uses the PostgreSQL adapter.

The schema contains Better Auth user/session/account/verification tables, Photo metadata and processing state, and PhotoProcessingOutbox. Photo indexes include user ownership, per-user SHA and perceptual hashes, processing state/start time, and deletion marker. Originals and derivatives are files on a PVC; the database stores storage keys and metadata, not photo bytes.

Migrations are committed under packages/db/prisma/migrations. See migration workflow, replication status, sharding status, and backup gaps.

docs.title: Current state
docs.text:
Replication is not implemented in the current manifests. PostgreSQL runs as a single-replica StatefulSet with one PVC. No streaming replication, standby, replication slot, WAL archive, failover controller, or managed database configuration was found.

A StatefulSet provides stable Pod identity and storage claims; increasing its replicas field would create separate PostgreSQL processes and does not configure them as primary/standby replicas. Do not scale this StatefulSet as a replication procedure.

docs.title: Future design questions
docs.text: A replication proposal must choose synchronous/asynchronous behavior, primary election/failover, WAL retention, backup integration, read routing, recovery objectives, and how Prisma migrations execute exactly once. Evaluate a PostgreSQL operator or managed HA database before implementing custom replication. Test failover and restore on disposable data first.

docs.title: Current state
docs.text:
Sharding is not implemented. Current code connects one Prisma client to one PostgreSQL database. Schema keys and queries are not documented as shard-aware; no routing layer, shard key, distributed transaction behavior, or Citus extension is configured in current manifests.

Git history/context notes that Citus was explored experimentally and was not retained as a validated architecture. The current repo does not establish a working Citus deployment or operational sharding path. Do not treat that experiment as a feature.

docs.title: Future work
docs.text: Before sharding, measure whether a single PostgreSQL instance is the limiting factor. A design would need a shard key (likely user ownership, but this is only a candidate), cross-shard query semantics, rebalancing, migrations, backup/restore, and operational observability. Replication and sharding solve different problems and neither is supplied by multiple Kubernetes Pods.

docs.title: Architecture decision records
docs.text:
These lightweight records summarize choices visible in code and configuration. Where no formal decision record was found, the rationale is stated as repository context or an inferred explanation, not as a confirmed historical decision.

  • ADR 0001: Kubernetes and environment namespaces
  • ADR 0002: PostgreSQL and Prisma
  • ADR 0003: Redis and BullMQ
  • ADR 0004: Citus experiment

docs.title: ADR 0001: Kubernetes and environment namespaces
docs.text: Status: Adopted in repository configuration; live operational status not independently verified.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The project targets self-hosted deployment on K3s and needs isolated Dev, Test, and Production configuration plus containerized services.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use Kubernetes resources rendered with Kustomize, K3s for the on-premise cluster setup, Traefik Ingress, and clichy-dev, clichy-test, clichy-prod namespaces. Monitoring and Headlamp are separate cluster tools.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: No alternatives are recorded in a formal ADR. Docker Compose is provided for local Postgres/Redis only, not as a production runtime.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Kubernetes supplies scheduling, service discovery, probes and Deployment rollouts. Operators must manage cluster access, PVCs, secrets, ingress, and node/storage availability. Namespaces isolate names and configuration but do not provide separate cluster failure domains.

docs.title: ADR 0002: PostgreSQL and Prisma
docs.text: Status: Adopted.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The API needs relational persistence for identity, ownership, photo metadata, and processing state.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use PostgreSQL with Prisma schema and committed migrations. Better Auth uses Prisma's PostgreSQL adapter. Each Kubernetes namespace has one PostgreSQL StatefulSet/Service and PVC.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: No alternatives are recorded in repository history available here.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Prisma provides typed data access and migration history. Schema migrations must be applied to independent environment databases. The current single instance is a single database availability/failure point; replication, sharding, backups and Test refresh are not implemented.

docs.title: ADR 0003: Redis and BullMQ for photo jobs
docs.text: Status: Adopted for asynchronous photo processing; operational baseline recorded at bce6e50, current live state not checked.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Uploads need image metadata extraction, hashing, and derivative generation without keeping the HTTP request open during all processing.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use BullMQ backed by Redis. Server creates queue jobs; worker consumes process-photo; a PostgreSQL outbox stores publication intent and enables retry/recovery.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: No formal comparison is recorded. Synchronous processing was avoided in favor of asynchronous work, based on current architecture.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Retries, backoff, queue identity and recovery behavior are explicit. Redis remains a single instance with AOF/PVC, so it has no configured failover. Shared filesystem access between API and worker is required.

docs.title: ADR 0004: Citus sharding experiment
docs.text: Status: Rejected/abandoned experiment; not current architecture.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Project-provided history says Citus was introduced experimentally to explore PostgreSQL sharding, encountered problems, and was not retained as a validated design.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: The current repository uses standard PostgreSQL and does not configure Citus. No operational sharding claims should be made.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Current single PostgreSQL instance is the implemented baseline. A formal comparison or exact experiment commit is not available in the checked-out history reviewed here.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The application has no shard routing or distributed transaction model. Future scaling should start with measured evidence and a documented design. Citus failure root cause and precise experiment outcomes remain unverified.

docs.title: ADR 0005: Traefik as ingress controller
docs.text: Status: Configured by K3s defaults and repository Ingress resources.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Browser traffic needs host/path routing to UI and API, while cluster services remain internal.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use Traefik's traefik IngressClass; base Clichy ingress uses the web entrypoint. K3s installer retains default Traefik installation.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: No controller comparison was found.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: K3s defaults make initial on-premise setup simpler. Hostnames, TLS, DNS and external exposure remain environment-specific; current Clichy Ingress does not configure TLS.

docs.title: ADR 0006: Environment namespaces
docs.text: Status: Adopted in overlays.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Test and Production need distinct settings, credentials and databases; Dev is configured separately.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use namespace-per-environment with independent resources, Secrets, URLs and PostgreSQL databases. CI deploys Test before Production.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Separate clusters are not configured. No formal alternatives record was found.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Namespace separation reduces accidental cross-environment naming/configuration overlap but shares the same cluster/node and does not guarantee resource/failure isolation. Test-to-Production promotion is ordered by workflow dependencies, but explicit application validation/approval depends partly on GitHub Environment settings.

docs.title: ADR 0007: No database replication or sharding in current baseline
docs.text: Status: Current configuration fact; revisit if measured needs justify a design.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Assignment asks for replication and sharding, but current repository config has one PostgreSQL StatefulSet replica and no Citus or replica configuration.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Document these as gaps, not implemented features. Do not scale StatefulSet replicas to simulate database HA.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: A PostgreSQL operator/managed service and Citus were not implemented in current tree; design alternatives remain open.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Single-instance database operations are simpler but have availability/capacity limitations. A future implementation requires failover, recovery, migration and validation procedures.

docs.title: ADR 0008: Zero-downtime rollout is not yet verified
docs.text: Status: Open evaluation criterion.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Kubernetes Deployments roll Pods, and deployment scripts wait for rollout completion. Default app replicas are one, and schema changes run before app manifests are updated.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Describe rolling update capability as configured but do not claim zero downtime without an observed test.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text: Multiple replicas and explicit rollout strategy can improve availability but must account for shared storage and database schema compatibility; no completed demonstration is recorded.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: A controlled deployment test with health checks, concurrent requests, metrics and a migration is needed before claiming the requirement is met.

docs.title: Clichy brand guidelines
docs.text: Clichy is a private home for personal photo collections. The identity should feel calm, personal, carefully organized, and trustworthy; photographs remain the most expressive part of the product.

docs.title: Logo
docs.text:
The symbol combines an open letter C with two offset image frames. The frames suggest a collection without using a literal camera or aperture illustration. Use the full lockup when the wordmark is needed and the symbol for compact places such as the favicon.

Assets live in apps/web/public/brand/:

  • logo-light.svg: charcoal lockup for warm, light surfaces.
  • logo-dark.svg: ivory lockup for dark surfaces.
  • symbol.svg: standalone charcoal symbol.
  • apps/web/public/favicon.svg: standalone symbol for browser and application tabs.
  • apps/web/src/components/brand-logo.tsx: reusable, theme-aware React logo.

Keep the logo at its original proportions, leave clear space around it, and do not recolor, skew, outline, or add effects to the SVG assets. The React logo uses the active theme's foreground and background colors.

docs.title: Color
docs.text:
The palette pairs warm paper and charcoal with a restrained sage accent and a small clay highlight:

Role Light theme Dark theme Use Background Warm ivory Deep warm charcoal Main canvas Foreground Charcoal Soft ivory Text and primary mark Primary Deep sage Light sage Main actions and active navigation Accent Muted clay Soft clay Small highlights, never large surfaces Secondary Pale sage/stone Deep sage/stone Quiet controls and selected surfaces Destructive Accessible red Accessible light red Permanent or destructive actions

Semantic success, warning, border, muted, and focus colors are also defined as CSS variables in packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css. Prefer semantic tokens such as bg-background, text-muted-foreground, and text-destructive over hard-coded colors.

docs.title: Typography
docs.text: Use the existing system sans-serif stack for controls and supporting text, with a restrained serif accent for large collection titles. The UI does not fetch fonts from a third-party host. Keep headings short and legible; use uppercase tracking sparingly for small section labels.

docs.title: Layout and components
docs.text:
• Let the photographs carry color and personality; use quiet surfaces around them.
  • Use consistent, generous spacing, with compact controls near the gallery.
  • Use rounded image corners and soft, rounded controls; avoid nested bordered cards and heavy shadows.
  • Reserve shadows for overlays and transient elevation.
  • Use Lucide icons with consistent stroke weight and pair icons with visible or screen-reader labels.
  • Keep destructive actions explicit and visually distinct.
  • Make focus states visible and preserve comfortable touch targets on mobile.

docs.title: Themes and motion
docs.text: Light and dark modes share the same semantic hierarchy. Use the theme tokens so text, surfaces, borders, and focus rings remain legible in either mode. Avoid theme-specific imagery or color-only status indicators. Honor prefers-reduced-motion; transitions should remain subtle and optional.

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
Local service orchestration is split: packages/db/docker-compose.yml starts PostgreSQL and Redis; root Turbo scripts run web, server, and worker processes. There is no root Compose file orchestrating all application services.

The expected development sequence is:

pnpm db:start
pnpm db:generate
pnpm db:migrate
pnpm dev

The API listens on port 3000 in apps/server/src/index.ts. The worker exposes health on port 3001. The React Router dev server chooses its local port and reports it at startup. The browser API URL is controlled by VITE_SERVER_URL.

For an isolated service, run pnpm dev:web, pnpm dev:server, or pnpm dev:worker. Keep API and worker pointed at the same PHOTO_STORAGE_PATH; otherwise the worker cannot read originals or the API cannot serve generated derivatives. This local filesystem coordination is also required in Kubernetes.

Use database migration commands for development changes; do not use db:push as a substitute for a committed migration workflow when schema history matters. Use pnpm db:studio to inspect records locally. Local startup has not been executed as part of this documentation pass.

docs.title: 1. Install tools and dependencies
docs.text:
Install Node.js 24, pnpm 12.8.1, Git, and Docker with Compose. Then clone the repository and install dependencies:

git clone https://github.com/valatras/clichy.git
cd clichy
corepack enable
corepack prepare pnpm@12.8.1 --activate
pnpm install

pnpm install triggers Varlock code generation through the root postinstall script. It does not start services.

docs.title: 2. Start local dependencies
docs.text:
pnpm db:start

This invokes the database workspace's docker compose up -d, starting PostgreSQL and Redis with named local volumes. The compose file exposes ports 5432 and 6379 on the host. Its sample PostgreSQL password is for local development only; do not reuse it elsewhere.

Configure local environment files based on the .env.schema files. Use a local PostgreSQL URL targeting database clichy, and set API/worker Redis host to 127.0.0.1. Provide a unique Better Auth secret of at least 32 characters and matching local auth/CORS URLs. Never copy production Secret values.

docs.title: 3. Prepare Prisma and run services
docs.text:
pnpm db:generate
pnpm db:migrate
pnpm dev

db:generate creates the Prisma client. db:migrate runs prisma migrate dev and may prompt to create/apply local migrations. pnpm dev runs package dev tasks through Turbo; use pnpm dev:web, pnpm dev:server, or pnpm dev:worker for an individual service. Confirm Vite's printed URL and that VITE_SERVER_URL points to the API.

docs.title: 4. Useful commands
docs.text:
pnpm check-types
pnpm --filter server test
pnpm --filter worker test
pnpm build
pnpm db:studio
pnpm db:stop
pnpm db:down

These names are defined in root/workspace manifests. db:stop stops containers but preserves volumes; db:down removes Compose containers/network but leaves named volumes unless -v is explicitly passed (which is not part of the script).

For image builds, use the existing Dockerfiles with repository root as build context:

docker build -f infra/docker_clichy_server/Dockerfile -t clichy-server:local .
docker build -f infra/docker_clichy_web/Dockerfile -t clichy-web:local .
docker build -f infra/docker_clichy_worker/Dockerfile -t clichy-worker:local .

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Prisma client missing: run pnpm db:generate after install/schema changes.
  • Connection refused: check docker compose ps in packages/db, then check ports and URLs.
  • Login fails locally: check BETTER_AUTH_URL, CORS_ORIGIN, secret length, and browser API URL alignment.
  • Worker reports no Redis: check Redis host/port/credentials and that worker shares the same queue name as the server.
  • Generated environment types missing: run pnpm env:generate after schema changes.
  • Avoid pnpm db:reset unless you intend to drop and recreate the local database.

docs.title: Toolchain
docs.text:
The root package.json pins pnpm@12.8.1; CI uses Node.js 24. The repository uses TypeScript, Turborepo, Varlock, Prisma, and Docker. Local database services are PostgreSQL 18 and Redis 7.4 from packages/db/docker-compose.yml. Docker Compose is needed for those services; Docker/Kubernetes are optional for app-only development.

Versions not pinned in repository metadata (for example, a local kubectl or mkdocs) must be selected by the operator. The K3s bootstrap script is specifically written for Ubuntu Server 24.04 and defaults to K3s v1.37.2+k3s1.

docs.title: Environment files
docs.text:
Schemas are in apps/web/.env.schema, apps/server/.env.schema, apps/worker/.env.schema, and packages/db/.env.schema. Root postinstall runs Varlock code generation. The server/worker require database and Redis connection settings; auth adds BETTER_AUTH_URL, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, CORS_ORIGIN; web uses VITE_SERVER_URL.

Variable Consumer Meaning/default evidence DATABASE_URL API, worker, Prisma PostgreSQL URL; required by server/worker BETTER_AUTH_SECRET API Required secret, schema min 32 characters BETTER_AUTH_URL API Auth canonical URL CORS_ORIGIN API Allowed browser origin PHOTO_STORAGE_PATH API/worker Defaults in schemas to local data paths; Kubernetes sets /data/photos REDIS_HOST, REDIS_PORT, REDIS_DB API/worker Defaults in code to 127.0.0.1, 6379, 0 REDIS_PASSWORD, REDIS_TLS API/worker Optional password and TLS toggle PHOTO_QUEUE_NAME API/worker Defaults to photo-processing PHOTO_JOB_ATTEMPTS, PHOTO_JOB_BACKOFF_MS Queue Defaults to 4 and 2000 ms PHOTO_WORKER_CONCURRENCY Worker Default 1; code permits 1 or 2 VITE_SERVER_URL Web build API base URL; currently build workflow supplies localhost URL

Never commit .env files or real secrets. The deploy scripts create Kubernetes Secrets interactively; see namespace setup.

docs.title: Project structure
docs.text:
Path Responsibility apps/web React Router UI apps/server Fastify API, photo storage and processing primitives, metrics, outbox dispatcher apps/worker BullMQ photo processing consumer and health listener packages/auth Better Auth configuration packages/db Prisma schema/client, migrations, local Postgres/Redis Compose packages/jobs Redis connection and BullMQ queue contracts/defaults packages/ui Shared UI components and styles packages/config Shared TypeScript configuration infra/docker_* Service Dockerfiles infra/kubernetes/base Shared Kubernetes resources infra/kubernetes/overlays Dev/Test/Prod Kustomize overlays infra/kubernetes/scripts Cluster, namespace, deployment, migration, monitoring and Headlamp scripts .github/workflows/ci.yml CI, GHCR packaging, Test and Production deploy jobs docs/ MkDocs source plus existing design/operations documentation

The root is a pnpm workspace coordinated by Turborepo. Package scripts are authoritative for runnable commands; consult package.json files before using a command not listed here.

docs.title: Testing and build checks
docs.text:
The repository uses Node's built-in test runner through tsx. Server tests cover storage, metrics, image processing, photo queries/routes, and outbox dispatch. Worker tests cover job processing behavior.

pnpm check-types
pnpm --filter server test
pnpm --filter worker test
pnpm build

CI uses the same commands after pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, with Node 24. Type checking receives a placeholder DATABASE_URL and web server URL; tests/build may depend on package environment configuration. The workflow does not run a dedicated lint task despite a root Turbo lint task definition.

For focused debugging, execute the package script or the test file via its package runner, for example pnpm --filter server exec tsx --test src/image-processing.test.ts. No test command has been run during this documentation edit; see the validation report for documentation build status.

docs.title: CI/CD pipeline
docs.text:
The single workflow is .github/workflows/ci.yml, triggered by pushes and pull requests to master.

flowchart TD
  Push[Push or PR to master] --> CI[Install frozen deps; typecheck; server tests; worker tests; build]
  CI -->|success| Images[Build server/web/worker images]
  Images -->|push to master| GHCR[Publish sha-<commit> tags]
  Images -->|PR| BuildOnly[Build only, no publish]
  GHCR --> Test[Self-hosted runner: verify SHA + single valtask node]
  Test --> TestMigrate[Prisma migrate deploy to Test]
  TestMigrate --> TestApply[Apply Test manifests and await rollouts]
  TestApply --> ProdGate[GitHub production Environment]
  ProdGate --> ProdMigrate[Prisma migrate deploy to Production]
  ProdMigrate --> ProdApply[Apply Production manifests and await rollouts]

docs.title: Sequence and gates
docs.text:
1. CI uses GitHub-hosted Ubuntu, pnpm action, Node 24 and frozen lockfile. It runs pnpm check-types, server tests, worker tests, and pnpm build.
  2. Packaging builds three Docker images from root context and service Dockerfiles. Only push-to-master logs into GHCR and pushes tags ghcr.io/valatras/clichy-{server,web,worker}:sha-${GITHUB_SHA}. Pull requests build without publishing.
  3. Test deploy runs on a self-hosted Linux runner. It requires checked-out SHA to equal workflow SHA and exactly one cluster node named valtask. It applies monitoring manifests, runs deploy.sh test sha-..., and reports resources even on failure.
  4. Production depends on CI, package, and Test deploy; uses GitHub Environment production, then runs the same exact-SHA checks and deploy script for prod.
  5. deploy.sh invokes migration first. If migration fails, application manifests are not applied. On success it renders the overlay with the SHA, applies it, then waits up to five minutes for server, web, and worker rollouts.

GitHub Environment review/approval is not configured in the YAML; it may be configured in repository settings. There is no separate human validation job, explicit Test smoke-test step, or automatic rollback job. A failing rollout stops the job, but rollback is an operator action. No zero-downtime demonstration is included.

docs.title: Migration workflow detail
docs.text: migrate.sh verifies a clean checked-out migration/deployment source, verifies node valtask, reads the environment Secret's DATABASE_URL without printing it, port-forwards PostgreSQL to a loopback ephemeral port, performs a PostgreSQL protocol SELECT 1, then invokes prisma migrate deploy (or prisma migrate status). It unsets credentials and cleans up the port-forward. It runs before new app manifests, so migrations must be compatible with currently running code during that interval.

docs.title: Cloud migration plan (not yet tested)
docs.text: There is no cloud-specific overlay or validated provider deployment in the repository. This page is a planning checklist, not an executable runbook.

docs.title: Portable parts
docs.text: Container images and tags, application Deployments, Services, Prisma migration model, queue contract, health endpoints, and most Kustomize structure are portable. The CI workflow can publish images to GHCR independent of runtime provider, but its self-hosted runner and kubeconfig currently target a host named valtask and enforce a single node.

docs.title: Provider-dependent work
docs.text: Area Current assumption Migration decision/work Storage Local PVs/node paths in Prod; local-path in other cluster Choose CSI block/file storage, access modes, snapshots, encryption, reclaim behavior; migrate data and validate API/worker shared photo access. PostgreSQL In-cluster single StatefulSet and PVC Decide managed database vs operator; update Secret/DNS/TLS/network policy; test restore and Prisma connectivity. Redis Single in-cluster Redis with PVC/AOF Decide managed Redis or replicated service; update TLS/auth and availability behavior. Ingress/load balancer K3s Traefik, host-based rules Choose managed LB/controller, configure health checks, public/private access, TLS and forwarding headers. DNS Local/LAN and existing hostname config Set authoritative records and certificate issuance; validate auth callback/CORS origin. Secrets Kubernetes Secrets made by scripts Move to cloud secret manager or sealed/external secret controller; rotate secrets and limit access. Registry GHCR Configure cloud cluster pull access and image policy; keep immutable SHA references. Monitoring kube-prometheus-stack with PVCs Size persistent metrics, retention, alert routing, egress and external monitoring needs. Network single-node K3s and ClusterIP services Design subnets, firewall rules, egress, private DB access, and pod/service CIDRs. Cost/sizing small fixed resource requests/limits Load test image processing and storage; size CPU, memory, IOPS, snapshots, egress and HA by measured demand.

docs.title: Safe migration sequence to design
docs.text:
1. Select provider and decide managed vs in-cluster PostgreSQL/Redis.
  2. Provision cluster, CSI storage, secrets integration, ingress, DNS and monitoring in a separate environment.
  3. Build and push a pinned SHA image; apply schema migrations using a reviewed compatible migration.
  4. Restore a sanitized Test dataset and verify auth, uploads, derivatives, queue recovery, metrics, and rollback procedure.
  5. Plan photo file migration and database consistency checks; preserve originals and verify hashes.
  6. Exercise failover, backup restore, rolling update and zero-downtime criteria before any production cutover.

These steps require environment-specific manifests and operational validation before becoming a production procedure.

docs.title: Scope and prerequisites
docs.text:
infra/kubernetes/scripts/install-k3s.sh targets Ubuntu Server 24.04, installs the K3s version declared by K3S_VERSION (default v1.37.2+k3s1), and retains K3s defaults including Traefik and local-path storage. It creates a user-owned kubeconfig (default ~/.kube/config-k3s) with mode 0600. It does not configure firewall rules, SSH, a multi-node cluster, or cloud resources.

Other scripts install Helm, prepare namespaces/secrets, install monitoring, configure LAN access, and install Headlamp. Read each script and confirm the selected kube context before running it: several scripts prompt before mutation, and namespace preparation for Production requires a mounted /srv/clichy filesystem.

docs.title: On-premise flow
docs.text:
1. Prepare an Ubuntu 24.04 host and verify storage/network prerequisites.
  2. Run infra/kubernetes/scripts/install-k3s.sh as the non-root operator account.
  3. Set KUBECONFIG to the generated kubeconfig and confirm kubectl get nodes.
  4. Install Helm with infra/kubernetes/scripts/install-helm.sh if needed.
  5. Prepare each namespace with infra/kubernetes/scripts/prepare-namespace.sh dev|test|prod; this creates local secret files and Kubernetes Secrets.
  6. Install monitoring with infra/kubernetes/scripts/install-monitoring.sh.
  7. Deploy application through CI or the exact SHA deploy script; details are in deployment.

The scripts are operational instructions, not proof that a clean host bootstrap was recently exercised. Production local PV manifests require node valtask and paths under /srv/clichy/k3s-storage/prod; generic cloud/local clusters do not satisfy these assumptions.

docs.title: Local development cluster
docs.text: The Dev overlay targets clichy.localhost, local/dev image tags, and one replica each. The repository does not provide a dedicated local cluster creation tool beyond K3s installer and the Dev Kustomize overlay. Build and load images into a chosen cluster yourself; this exact workflow is not automated in repository scripts.

docs.title: Kubernetes implementation
docs.text: Kustomize base resources are under infra/kubernetes/base; environment overlays are under infra/kubernetes/overlays/{dev,test,prod}. Common resources include web/API/worker Deployments, Services, PostgreSQL StatefulSet/Service, Redis Deployment/Service/PVC, photo PVC, and Ingress.

docs.title: Workload behavior
docs.text:
• API and web use readiness/liveness HTTP checks on /; worker health listener is on 3001 but the Deployment currently has no probe configured.
  • PostgreSQL uses a one-replica StatefulSet and a 10 GiB claim template.
  • Redis uses a one-replica Deployment, AOF, noeviction, 256 MiB maxmemory, probes, and a PVC.
  • API, worker, web and database have CPU/memory requests and limits in base manifests.
  • Test adds CPU HPA for API and web (1–4 replicas, 70% utilization target). Dev and Production specify one replica for web/server/worker. Production does not include this HPA.
  • Deploy script applies manifests and waits for each app Deployment rollout, but does not explicitly check StatefulSet or HPA convergence.

Kubernetes Deployment rollout is not itself proof of zero downtime. One-replica app workloads, storage attachment, readiness behavior, schema compatibility, and live traffic need a measured rollout test.

docs.title: Environment differences
docs.text:
Dev uses clichy.localhost, development NODE_ENV, and local image names. Test uses clichy-test.home.arpa, GHCR images, hardened app security context, image pull secret, and HPA. Production uses valtask.xyz, exact SHA image tags, hardened contexts, production secrets, local PVs and one replica. All share the base architecture while namespaces and Secrets isolate resources.

Render without applying to inspect an overlay:

kubectl kustomize infra/kubernetes/overlays/test

This requires kubectl with Kustomize support. Do not apply a rendered overlay until its namespace, secrets, image references, storage, and target cluster are reviewed.

docs.title: Prometheus and Grafana
docs.text:
infra/kubernetes/scripts/install-monitoring.sh installs kube-prometheus-stack chart version 93.1.1 by default into namespace monitoring. It creates/uses a Grafana admin Secret, persistent Grafana and Prometheus storage, seven-day Prometheus retention, kube-state-metrics, node-exporter, and Alertmanager.

infra/kubernetes/monitoring/service-monitor.yaml scrapes server /metrics every 30 seconds in clichy-dev and clichy-test; it does not include Prod. Server registers application metrics in apps/server/src/metrics.ts. Kubernetes resource/workload metrics are supplied by the monitoring stack. A Grafana dashboard JSON and Prometheus rules are checked in. Live scrape health and dashboard import were not verified during this review.

Useful checks:

kubectl get pods,servicemonitors,prometheusrules -n monitoring
kubectl get servicemonitor clichy-server -n monitoring -o yaml
kubectl get pods -n monitoring -o wide

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
Test has CPU HPAs for server and web, target 70% average CPU utilization, minimum one and maximum four replicas. No HPA exists for worker, Redis, or PostgreSQL. HPA needs functioning resource metrics and CPU requests; manifests provide requests, but metrics-server availability is not established by an HPA YAML alone.

kubectl get hpa -n clichy-test
kubectl describe hpa clichy-server -n clichy-test
kubectl top pods -n clichy-test
kubectl scale deployment/clichy-worker --replicas=2 -n clichy-test
kubectl rollout status deployment/clichy-worker -n clichy-test

Manual scaling examples change live cluster state. Review capacity, shared volume access, and queue behavior first. Avoid scaling PostgreSQL or Redis by changing replicas: their current manifests do not implement data replication or clustered coordination.

Troubleshoot HPA with kubectl describe hpa, kubectl get apiservice v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io, kubectl top nodes, and Pod CPU requests. Headlamp is an optional Kubernetes UI installed by dedicated scripts/RBAC; it is not application monitoring.

docs.title: Namespaces
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  Public[Browser: valtask.xyz / www.valtask.xyz] --> CF[Cloudflare edge and Tunnel]
  subgraph Cluster[K3s cluster]
    subgraph Dev[clichy-dev]
      D[web + server + worker + PostgreSQL + Redis]
    end
    subgraph Test[clichy-test]
      T[web + server + worker + PostgreSQL + Redis + HPA]
    end
    subgraph Prod[clichy-prod]
      P[web + server + worker + PostgreSQL + Redis]
    end
    subgraph Monitoring[monitoring]
      M[Prometheus + Grafana + Alertmanager]
    end
    subgraph Headlamp[headlamp]
      H[Headlamp UI]
    end
    Traefik[Cluster Traefik]
  end
  CF -->|valtask.xyz over HTTP to web :80; www redirects to valtask.xyz| Traefik
  Traefik -->|host rules| Dev
  Traefik -->|host rules| Test
  Traefik -->|valtask.xyz| Prod
  M -. scrapes .-> Dev
  M -. scrapes .-> Test

Each clichy-* namespace contains independent workload Services, database, Redis, generated ConfigMaps, and environment Secrets. There is no data replication between namespaces. Monitoring's Clichy ServiceMonitor selects Dev and Test only; it does not scrape Production application metrics in this manifest. The Grafana dashboard can query namespace variables, but actual production metric visibility depends on the scrape configuration.

Production's public route enters through Cloudflare Tunnel to Traefik; www.valtask.xyz redirects at Cloudflare to the canonical valtask.xyz host. The tunnel and redirect are external configuration and are not represented as Kubernetes resources in this repository.

headlamp has separate RBAC and Ingress manifests. The Monitoring/Headlamp manifests and scripts configure cluster tools; inspect their LAN hostnames and access policy before exposing them.

docs.title: Setup and inspection
docs.text:
infra/kubernetes/scripts/prepare-namespace.sh test
kubectl get all,pvc,ingress -n clichy-test
kubectl get secret -n clichy-test

Secret listing shows names only. Do not print Secret data into logs or paste it into documentation. The setup script asks for database and GHCR credentials and stores a local protected env file under $HOME/.config/clichy.

docs.title: Claims and paths
docs.text:
Base defines a 10 GiB PostgreSQL volume claim template, a 10 GiB photos PVC, and a 1 GiB Redis PVC. PostgreSQL and Redis data survive Pod replacement only if the claim is bound to durable storage. Dev/Test rely on cluster default storage class unless overridden. Production declares clichy-prod-local with kubernetes.io/no-provisioner, WaitForFirstConsumer, local PVs and node affinity to valtask.

The production local PV definitions specify host paths under /srv/clichy/k3s-storage/prod/{postgres,photos,redis} and Retain reclaim policy. The namespace preparation script checks /srv/clichy is mounted and prepares these directories. The known-issues record states current PVCs still use existing local-path storage at the time of that incident; current manifests now declare the production local StorageClass. This repository-level config and historical note differ in time, so inspect actual bound PVs before data operations.

The server and worker mount the photos claim at /data/photos. They must see the same files. Access mode is ReadWriteOnce; this is often node-scoped rather than multi-node shared storage, and does not establish safe cross-node scheduling. Production is explicitly tied to one node.

docs.title: Operational checks
docs.text:
kubectl get pvc,pv -n clichy-prod -o wide
kubectl describe pvc clichy-server-photos -n clichy-prod
kubectl describe statefulset clichy-postgres -n clichy-prod

No database backup/restore automation is present in the inspected repository. Retain prevents Kubernetes from automatically deleting PV data on claim release but is not a backup. See backup and restore.

docs.title: Automated deployment
docs.text: Push to master triggers CI, image builds, Test deployment and then Production deployment, as described in CI/CD. Deployment uses exact commit SHA tags. The self-hosted runner must have access to the target K3s kubeconfig, kubectl, Node 24, pnpm, GHCR, and namespace secrets. The script refuses to run unless the cluster reports exactly one node named valtask.

docs.title: Manual checked-out SHA deployment
docs.text:
From a clean checkout that matches the published images:

CLICHY_DEPLOY_CONFIRM=yes ./infra/kubernetes/scripts/deploy.sh test sha-<40-character-commit-sha>
CLICHY_DEPLOY_CONFIRM=yes ./infra/kubernetes/scripts/deploy.sh prod sha-<40-character-commit-sha>

Use manual commands only when the selected image tag exists and git rev-parse HEAD matches it. Production deploy additionally checks required Secret keys and GHCR pull-secret type. The script migrates first, renders manifests into a temporary Kustomize directory, applies the environment, waits for API/web/worker rollouts, and prints workload status. Without CLICHY_DEPLOY_CONFIRM=yes, it asks for interactive confirmation.

docs.title: Before/after checks
docs.text:
kubectl config current-context
kubectl get nodes
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh test status
kubectl get deployments,pods,pvc,ingress -n clichy-test -o wide
kubectl rollout history deployment/clichy-server -n clichy-test

After a failure, inspect kubectl describe, events, Pod logs, migration status, and PostgreSQL logs before retrying. There is no automated rollback step. Do not delete PVCs or reset the database to address rollout failures. A deliberate rollback would need a compatible prior image SHA and an operator review of schema compatibility; the repo does not provide a turnkey rollback script.

docs.title: Known issues and resolved incidents
docs.text: This is a record of issues evidenced by current documentation, source, or Git history. Absence of an open item here does not mean the system has been tested comprehensively.

docs.title: Production database missing Prisma tables
docs.text: Status: Resolved (2026-11-14) Affected component: Production Better Auth / PostgreSQL deployment Symptoms: Account registration returned HTTP 500 and logs reported Prisma P2021, missing public.user. Root cause: The new Production database had not received migrations. Earlier deployment automation migrated Test but not Production. Resolution: Applied pending 20261005225922_adding_photos_objects migration to Production using prisma migrate deploy through a temporary loopback-only port-forward. Registration then worked. Verification: The contemporaneous operations record reports Prisma schema up to date and a successful account creation; this is historical execution evidence, not a current live check. Relevant files: infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh, infra/kubernetes/scripts/deploy.sh, .github/workflows/ci.yml, packages/db/prisma/migrations/. Related commits: c96c262 (“Fixing migration issue in prod and adding the migration process to ci/cd”), c3624d8 (Production deployment script); detailed incident record was already in docs/operations/known-issues.md before this documentation work.

docs.title: PostgreSQL connectivity and Prisma deployment stability
docs.text: Status: Historical fixes present; current operation unverified Affected component: Prisma, PostgreSQL Service and deployment scripts Symptoms: Commit history records 7e8f334 “fix connectivity issue between prisma and postgresql pod” and 21d2785 “fix: database to prisma connection stability.” Root cause: Not established by commit subjects alone. Current migration script uses a loopback port-forward, dynamically discovers its local port, and validates with a PostgreSQL protocol SELECT 1; exact earlier failure mechanism is not established. Resolution: Connectivity changes and a more defensive migration path are in the current tree. Verification: Source inspection only for this documentation pass. Relevant files: infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh, packages/db/src/, infra/kubernetes/base/postgres/. Related commits: 7e8f334, 21d2785.

docs.title: Citus sharding experiment
docs.text: Status: Historical experiment; not operational Affected component: Database architecture Symptoms: Project context supplied for this documentation task reports Citus was experimentally introduced, encountered problems, and was not retained. Root cause: Not verified from current repository or available commit subjects. Resolution: Current architecture is standard PostgreSQL plus Redis/BullMQ; current schema/manifests show no Citus deployment. Verification: Current manifests and package files inspected; a working Citus setup is absent. Relevant files: infra/kubernetes/base/postgres/, packages/db/. Related commits: No Citus-specific commit was identified in current master history search. Treat the experiment history as project-provided context until historical commits/docs are made available.

docs.title: Traefik Ingress routing corrections
docs.text: Status: Historical correction committed; current reachability unverified Affected component: Clichy and Headlamp Ingress Symptoms: Git history records a Traefik port/entrypoint correction and Headlamp Ingress namespace correction. Root cause: Commit message 637e762 says base Ingress did not explicitly select web, and Headlamp Ingress had been declared in default; details beyond that message are not established. Resolution: Base Clichy Ingress explicitly uses entrypoint web; Headlamp Ingress is in headlamp, and installer removes the earlier misplaced resource. Verification: Current manifest/source inspection only. Relevant files: infra/kubernetes/base/ingress.yaml, infra/kubernetes/headlamp/lan-ingress.yaml, infra/kubernetes/scripts/install-headlamp.sh. Related commit: 637e762.

docs.title: PostgreSQL data directory ownership
docs.text: Status: Current fix committed; live storage not verified Affected component: Production PostgreSQL StatefulSet and local PV setup Symptoms: Most recent commit title indicates a permissions issue for PostgreSQL UID 999. Root cause: The commit message establishes that the data directory permissions needed correction for UID 999; exact runtime symptom is not available from repository evidence. Resolution: Current prepare-namespace.sh checks/sets ownership for an empty PostgreSQL directory and 2a7717f adjusts ownership handling. It intentionally refuses unsafe recursive ownership changes on populated data. Verification: Source inspection; not tested against live volume. Relevant files: infra/kubernetes/scripts/prepare-namespace.sh, infra/kubernetes/base/postgres/statefulset.yaml. Related commits: 2a7717f, 4bceaff.

docs.title: Operational gaps (not recorded incidents)
docs.text: These are limitations established by configuration, not claims of past failures: no database backup/restore runbook, no PostgreSQL replication or sharding, one Redis instance, and no Test database refresh/anonymization procedure. See corresponding database pages and requirement matrix.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Start with namespace and context checks to avoid inspecting the wrong cluster:

kubectl config current-context
kubectl get nodes
kubectl get deployments,pods,services,endpoints,pvc,ingress -n clichy-test -o wide
kubectl get events -n clichy-test --sort-by=.lastTimestamp
Symptom Checks Pod pending / PVC pending kubectl describe pod, kubectl describe pvc; verify StorageClass, local PV node affinity and node path. ImagePullBackOff Check image tag and ghcr-pull-secret exists in the workload namespace; never display its data. API can't connect PostgreSQL Check PostgreSQL Pod readiness/logs, Service endpoints, DATABASE_URL Secret presence/key name, and namespace match. Use migrate.sh <env> status for a protocol-aware DB check. Migration fails Read workflow/script output and PostgreSQL logs; run migration status; do not reset DB or remove PVC. Upload returns 400/413 Check supported format and 20 MiB multipart cap; image decoder also caps at 40 million pixels. Photo stays pending Inspect worker readiness/logs, Redis connectivity, queue name, outbox rows and photo storage mount. The worker Deployment has no Kubernetes probe despite exposing port 3001. Thumbnail missing Confirm photo belongs to user, processing completed, derivative exists on shared volume, and API/worker mount same PVC. HPA has unknown metrics Inspect HPA events, metrics APIService, kubectl top pods, CPU requests and monitoring separately. Prometheus does not itself guarantee the Kubernetes resource metrics API required by HPA. Ingress unavailable Verify host DNS, Traefik, Ingress class/entrypoint, Service endpoints and whether TLS is configured for that host.

For logs: kubectl logs deployment/clichy-server -n clichy-test, kubectl logs deployment/clichy-worker -n clichy-test, and kubectl logs statefulset/clichy-postgres -n clichy-test. Use production namespace only with appropriate access and redact user data/secrets from any shared diagnostic output.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Meaning in this repository API Fastify service in apps/server Derivative Resized WebP preview stored beside photo data on shared filesystem Outbox PostgreSQL PhotoProcessingOutbox rows used to reliably publish work to Redis pHash Perceptual image hash generated from a 32×32 grayscale image using low-frequency DCT coefficients Hamming distance Number of differing bits between two 64-bit pHashes Overlay Kustomize environment-specific customization of base resources PVC / PV Kubernetes persistent volume claim / volume SHA Git commit SHA used as immutable image tag (sha-<40 hex chars>)

docs.title: Project overview
docs.text: Clichy is intended to help users ingest, browse, and manage personal photo collections. The checked-in application currently supports account authentication, photo upload and listing, metadata retrieval, thumbnail derivatives, deletion, and server-side image processing. Similarity primitives exist, but a finished duplicate-review workflow and video support are not evident in the current source.

docs.title: Architecture at a glance
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  Browser -->|HTTP| Ingress[Traefik Ingress]
  Ingress --> Web[React Router web]
  Ingress --> API[Fastify API]
  API --> DB[(PostgreSQL / Prisma)]
  API --> FS[(Shared photo filesystem)]
  API --> Redis[(Redis + BullMQ)]
  API --> Worker[Worker]
  Worker --> FS
  Worker --> DB
  Prom[Prometheus] -. scrapes /metrics .-> API

The API and worker mount the photo volume and share originals and derivatives. The API persists upload metadata and an outbox event; a dispatcher publishes queue jobs. The worker computes metadata, hashes, and derivatives.

docs.title: Technology stack
docs.text:
Area Repository evidence Web React, React Router, Vite, Tailwind CSS, shared @clichy/ui API Node.js, TypeScript, Fastify, Better Auth, multipart uploads Processing Sharp, Exifr, SHA-256, 64-bit perceptual hash, BullMQ Data PostgreSQL 18, Prisma 7, pg adapter Queue Redis 7.4, BullMQ 5, ioredis Packaging pnpm 12 workspace, Turborepo, Docker Runtime Kubernetes/K3s manifests, Kustomize, Traefik Operations GitHub Actions, GHCR, kube-prometheus-stack, Grafana, Headlamp

Versions shown in manifests and package files are the repository's declarations and can differ from what is installed on a live host.

docs.title: Status summary
docs.text:
Capability Current repository status Authentication and account persistence Implemented; live operation not independently verified here Photo upload, ownership checks, local filesystem storage Implemented Image metadata and derivatives Implemented for JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF Exact and perceptual similarity primitives Implemented; complete user-facing duplicate workflow not established Video ingestion Not implemented in inspected API pipeline Kubernetes deployment Manifests and scripts implemented; live state is not established by source review Test then Production automation Implemented in workflow; actual recent run status is not checked here Database replication / sharding Not implemented Zero-downtime rollout Intended by Deployment rolling update behavior, but not verified and replicas are one

See requirements traceability and roadmap for detail. Source locations are listed as repository-relative paths to make code review straightforward.

docs.title: Assignment requirements traceability
docs.text:
Statuses describe repository evidence at master (2a7717f), not an independent evaluation demo. “Implemented, not verified” means configuration or code is present but its operation was not observed in this review.

Requirement Status Evidence and gap Unit tests after push Implemented, not verified .github/workflows/ci.yml runs type checks, server and worker tests, then builds on pushes and PRs to master. Automatic deployment to Test after successful tests Implemented, not verified deploy-test follows CI and image packaging; self-hosted runner and cluster are required. Promote to Production after validation Partially implemented Production waits for Test deployment and uses GitHub production Environment. Workflow has no explicit validation job; environment protection/approval depends on GitHub settings, which are not versioned. Zero-downtime deployment Not verified Deployments use Kubernetes rolling update defaults, but each environment sets one replica. No demonstrated availability test or rollout evidence is versioned. Database sharding Not implemented One PostgreSQL StatefulSet, one replica. Citus is not part of current manifests or package dependencies. Database replication Not implemented No standby, replication slots, operator, or replication configuration found. One StatefulSet replica is not database replication. Schema migrations Implemented Prisma migrations in packages/db/prisma/migrations; migrate.sh runs prisma migrate deploy before manifests. Refresh Test from Production with anonymization Not implemented No dump/restore or anonymization procedure found. Multiple application Pods Partially implemented Deployments can support replicas, but Dev/Prod overlay counts are one; Test HPA can scale web and server up to four if metrics are available. Worker stays one. Replicated cache layer Not implemented One Redis Deployment, one replica, AOF persistence; no Redis replication/Sentinel/Cluster. Single Ingress exposing application Implemented One Clichy Ingress routes /api/auth, /photos to server and / to web. Traefik is cluster ingress class. Dashboard for system load and app health Implemented, not verified kube-prometheus-stack, Grafana dashboard JSON, API /metrics, Kubernetes alerts. Live scrape and dashboards not verified. Manual or automatic scaling Partially implemented Kubernetes supports manual scale; Test HPA manifests target server/web CPU. Metrics API availability and actual HPA behavior are unverified. Kubernetes rolling updates Implemented, not verified Kubernetes Deployments and rollout status checks in deploy script. No rollout demonstration evidence checked. Migration during update Implemented, not verified Test and Prod jobs run migration before applying application manifests. Local cluster setup Documented scripts exist install-k3s.sh targets Ubuntu 24.04; fresh install behavior not exercised here. Cloud migration guide Proposed in this site Provider migration is a planning guide only; no cloud overlay exists. CI/CD documentation Implemented in this site See pipeline. Database documentation Implemented in this site See database section; backup procedures are absent from repository. Monitoring/scaling documentation Implemented in this site See monitoring. Developer onboarding Implemented in this site Commands are cross-checked against scripts and package manifests; local execution has not been verified.

docs.title: Evaluation notes
docs.text: Key gaps for a demonstration are database replication and sharding, repeatable Test refresh with anonymization, proof of zero downtime, multi-replica application behavior, Redis availability, and a verified metrics/HPA path. Before marking configured features operational, capture workflow runs, cluster status, and a controlled rollout observation.

docs.title: Evidence-based progression
docs.text:
Git history shows a foundation and application development, followed by image hashing, Redis/BullMQ work, Kubernetes and monitoring changes, and a database migration/deployment repair. Not every historical experiment is part of the current runtime.

Stage Verified status 1. Foundation Historical; initial structure and local development are present. Exact completion criteria are not defined in current docs. 2. Authentication and storage Implemented: Better Auth/Prisma, per-user photo records, filesystem originals and derivatives. 3. Image processing Implemented baseline: EXIF extraction, dimensions, SHA-256, pHash, Hamming distance, WebP derivatives. Broader automated curation UX is incomplete/unverified. 4. Containerization Dockerfiles exist for web/server/worker; compose exists for PostgreSQL and Redis. 5. Kubernetes Kustomize base/overlays, K3s scripts, Ingress and storage manifests exist. Live cluster state is outside source review. 6. Asynchronous processing Functional baseline intended at bce6e50; current source has BullMQ worker, retry settings, DB outbox and stale-job recovery. Current live operation is unverified. 7. Infrastructure and deployment improvements In progress: exact-SHA CI/CD, pre-deploy Prisma migrations, environment secrets, prod storage config, monitoring. Recent commits are still changing this area. 8. Paused stage On hold per project context. Exact stage name is not present in the checked-in plan/docs available in this checkout. 9.
